column1: # mdl-rule-kinds.tsv — which MDL rules a script needs, by the kind of statement it writes.
# Read by bin/mdl-rules.sh (and nothing else); rendered to skills/generated/rules-<kind>.md.
# WHY (lazy-load PR 2, 2026-10-23). The mdl helper preloaded every kind-specific skill at Stage 5
# (29,388 words), though a page script needs none of the microflow rules and a microflow script
# none of the page rules. This table says which sections each statement kind needs, so the helper
# loads them per script instead. The skills keep every word; only who preloads them changes.
# Sections are located by FILE plus HEADING TEXT, never by line number (the bin/lib/runbook-span.sh
# precedent): a heading matches when its text, after the leading #s, starts with the heading cell.
# A heading that no longer exists makes bin/mdl-rules.sh fail loudly — it never prints empty.
# Format: TAB-separated, four columns. Blank lines and #-comments ignored.
#   1 kind      page | microflow | access | workflow | entity | any   (any = every script)
#               top      everything above the file's first "## " heading
#               section  the heading and everything under it, down to the next heading of its level
#               stop     the STOP table under that heading, rows filtered by their Kind column
#                        (the kinds asked for, plus `any`; the retired-numbers row always)
#               bullet   one bullet under that heading: arg is "<heading>::<bullet lead text>"
#               rows     the table rows under that heading whose FIRST cell matches an ERE
#               exclude  kind "-": a `##` section deliberately reaching no kind (it is not a rule
#                        for writing MDL); arg is "<heading>::<one-line reason>"
#   4 arg       heading text, or heading::lead / heading::ERE / heading::reason as above; "-" for
# Denominators (bin/mdl-rules.sh --check): every STOP row carries a known Kind, every bullet under
# a `bullet` heading is selected by some row here, every table row under a `rows` heading is matched
# by some ERE here and every ERE matches some row on its own, every `##` section of a file read in
# parts (no `file` row) is selected or excluded below, and every generated file equals a fresh
# render. A new gotcha, register row or section that no kind selects fails --check, so it cannot
# silently stop reaching the mdl helper. Headings inside code fences are not headings.
